lines: A brass tally tag on a nail in a dead snag. Stamped: 'GAGE, No. 3'. A tag on the board means you came up. This one is not on the board.
You pocket the tag. It is lighter than it should be.
A tally tag in the ferns, polished by years of rain. 'MOLLY, No. 9'. Someone scratched a smile on the back.
You pocket the tag. It is lighter than it should be.
A tally tag tied to a rabbit snare. 'HAMM, No. 1, SHIFT BOSS'. The snare is empty. The rabbit won.
You pocket the tag. It is lighter than it should be.
A tally tag in a slag heap. 'PENN, No. 12'. Under it, older and smaller: 'PENN, No. 12, APPRENTICE'.
You pocket the tag. It is lighter than it should be.

tag_empty: Only a nail where a tag hung.

lines: A notice board, empty but for nails. A good spot for bad news.
You pin up one of Mercer's notices. 'Departed, suddenly, tomorrow.' The ink is still wet.

notice_1_plain: A notice board, empty but for nails. A good spot for bad news.

lines: A notice board leaning on a slag heap. Someone has carved 'WHO NEXT?' into it, then 'NOT ME'.
You pin up one of Mercer's notices. 'Departed, suddenly, tomorrow.' The ink is still wet.

sign: North: Cinderfold. South: the Bellows Deep, closed. In between: the Ash Assize, open, unfortunately.
deep_sign: BELLOWS DEEP - CLOSED BY ORDER OF THE RUSKWEBER CLAN.
Under it, newer: 'Wages still payable at the office below.'
clem: Clem: Juror number one. I was picked because I own a chair. Most of the heath doesn't.
clem_intro: Clem: My vote's for sale. The price is one duel. Inflation, you know.
clem_defeat: Clem: Sold. Tell Greaves I said guilty. Of whatever. He'll know.
mattie: Mattie: I've sat on forty juries. The verdict was always the same. I find that comforting.
mattie_intro: Mattie: Win my vote and I'll vote. It won't count, but I'll do it beautifully.
mattie_defeat: Mattie: My vote is yours. Keep the receipt.
dunstan: Dunstan: I'm on the jury because the clan owes me money. They pay me in verdicts.
dunstan_intro: Dunstan: Three votes down, two to go. Or three to go, if you lose to me. Do the maths.
dunstan_defeat: Dunstan: Fine. Vote cast. Into a very deep well, probably.
wick: Wick: I fell asleep during my last trial. I voted in my sleep. The defendant was hanged in effigy. The effigy was furious.
wick_intro: Wick: Wake me up, then. If you can.
wick_defeat: Wick: I'm up. I'm up. My vote's yours. What were we voting on?
ansa: Ansa: Foreman of the jury. I read the verdict out loud. Greaves writes it, I read it. It's a very good job. Low thinking.
ansa_intro: Ansa: Last vote. Make it count. It won't, but make it.
ansa_defeat: Ansa: Unanimous, then. Go and hear your verdict. Read the docket first. I'm not allowed to say that.
